notes.agrum: Reads the network's UAI file and its observations, the file Merlin reads.

notes.pgmpy: Reads the network's UAI file and its observations, the file Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the in-process time leaves it out.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. On the other programs it is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers the Dice programs exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added. On its own linear regression it answers the posterior means of the continuous model, E(a) and E(b), which the circuit's bit queries do not have, so there is nothing to compare them with.
notes.sppl: SPPL answers the continuous model, with normal emissions as densities; the circuit rounds them to a grid, so the differences from the reference are that discretization.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. On the other programs it is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.

using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const IGNORE_ERRORS = true

model() = @alea begin
    n = 6

    id = Vector(undef, n)
    for i in 1:n
        id[i] = uniform(DistUInt{7}, 0, 10)
    end

    id_obs = [2, 0, 5, 6, 0, 0]

    for i in 1:n
        observe(ifelse(flip(1/2), prob_equals(id[i], DistUInt{7}(id_obs[i])), true))
    end


    sum = DistUInt{7}(0)
    for i in 2:n
        if i % 2 == 0
            sum = sum + id[i]
        else
            sum = sum +  ifelse(id[i] > DistUInt{7}(4), DistUInt{7}(2) * id[i] - DistUInt{7}(9), DistUInt{7}(2) * id[i])
        end
    end

    mod = sum % DistUInt{7}(10)

    observe(prob_equals(id[1], DistUInt{7}(10)-mod))




    (id[1], id[2], id[3], id[4], id[5], id[6])
end

using Alea

model() = @alea begin
    n = 4

    id = Vector(undef, n)
    for i in 1:n
        id[i] = uniform(DistUInt{7}, 0, 10)
    end

    id_obs = [2, 0, 5, 6]

    for i in 1:n
        observe(ifelse(flip(1/2), prob_equals(id[i], DistUInt{7}(id_obs[i])), true))
    end

    for i in 2:n

        end
    end

    mod = sum % DistUInt{7}(10)

    observe(prob_equals(id[1], DistUInt{7}(10)-mod))




    (id[1], id[2], id[3], id[4])
end
